#
# Usage:

TIMEOUT="${HEALTHCHECK_TIMEOUT:-3}"   # seconds per check

  PORTS=("${DEFAULT_PORTS[@]}")
fi

  GREEN=''; RED=''; BOLD=''; RESET=''
fi

# check_port <port> -> 0 if responding, 1 otherwise
check_port() {
  local port="$1"

  # Prefer curl (verifies the port actually serves HTTP-ish responses),
  # fall back to a raw TCP connection via /dev/tcp if curl is unavailable.
  if command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then

            --connect-timeout "$TIMEOUT" --max-time "$TIMEOUT" \
            "http://${HOST}:${port}/" 2>/dev/null; then
      return 0
    fi
    return 1
  else
    # Bash TCP fallback: open a connection and immediately close it.
    if timeout "$TIMEOUT" bash -c "exec 3<>/dev/tcp/${HOST}/${port}" 2>/dev/null; then
      return 0
    fi
    return 1
  fi
}

# --- Run checks ---------------------------------------------------------------

echo -e "${BOLD}Health check — host: ${HOST}${RESET}"
echo "-------------------------------------------"

failures=0

for port in "${PORTS[@]}"; do
  if check_port "$port"; then
    printf "  port %-6s ${GREEN}UP${RESET}\n" "$port"
  else
    printf "  port %-6s ${RED}DOWN${RESET}\n" "$port"
    failures=$((failures + 1))
  fi
done

echo "-------------------------------------------"

if [[ "$failures" -eq 0 ]]; then
  echo -e "${GREEN}All services are up.${RESET}"
  exit 0
else
  echo -e "${RED}${failures} service(s) down.${RESET}"
  exit 1
fi

#
# healthcheck.sh - Check whether local services are responding.
#
# Probes a configurable list of host:port targets and reports their status.
# Exits 0 if all services are healthy, 1 if any are down.

set -u

# --- Configuration -----------------------------------------------------------

# Targets to check, in "name|host|port" format.
SERVICES=(
  "service-3000|127.0.0.1|3000"
  "service-8080|127.0.0.1|8080"
)

# How long (seconds) to wait for each connection attempt.
TIMEOUT="${HEALTHCHECK_TIMEOUT:-3}"

# Colors (only if stdout is a terminal).
if [ -t 1 ]; then
  GREEN=$'\033[0;32m'
  RED=$'\033[0;31m'
  BOLD=$'\033[1m'
  RESET=$'\033[0m'
else
  GREEN=""; RED=""; BOLD=""; RESET=""
fi

# check_port HOST PORT -> returns 0 if the port responds, 1 otherwise.
check_port() {
  local host="$1" port="$2"

  # Prefer a TCP connect via curl (widely available). curl returns:
  #   0  -> got an HTTP response
  #   7  -> connection refused / could not connect (service down)
  #   52 -> connected but empty reply (service up but not HTTP)
  #   28 -> timeout
  if command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    curl --silent --output /dev/null \
         --connect-timeout "$TIMEOUT" --max-time "$TIMEOUT" \
         "http://${host}:${port}/" 2>/dev/null
    local rc=$?
    # rc 0 = healthy HTTP response; rc 52 = connected (open port, non-HTTP)
    [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || [ "$rc" -eq 52 ]
    return $?
  fi

  # Fallback: raw TCP connect using bash's /dev/tcp pseudo-device.
  if (exec 3<>"/dev/tcp/${host}/${port}") 2>/dev/null; then
    exec 3>&- 3<&-
    return 0
  fi

  return 1
}

# --- Main --------------------------------------------------------------------

echo "${BOLD}Service health check${RESET} ($(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S'))"
echo "----------------------------------------"

overall=0

for entry in "${SERVICES[@]}"; do
  IFS='|' read -r name host port <<< "$entry"

  if check_port "$host" "$port"; then
    printf "  %-16s %s:%-5s  %sUP%s\n"   "$name" "$host" "$port" "$GREEN" "$RESET"
  else
    printf "  %-16s %s:%-5s  %sDOWN%s\n" "$name" "$host" "$port" "$RED" "$RESET"
    overall=1
  fi
done

echo "----------------------------------------"
if [ "$overall" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "${GREEN}All services healthy.${RESET}"
else
  echo "${RED}One or more services are down.${RESET}"
fi

exit "$overall"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# healthcheck.sh - Check whether local services are responding.
#
# Checks that the services listening on the configured ports are up by
# issuing a lightweight HTTP request to each. Reports per-service status
# and exits non-zero if any service is down.
#
# Usage:
#   ./healthcheck.sh                 # check default ports (3000 8080)
#   ./healthcheck.sh 3000 8080 9000  # check a custom list of ports
#   HOST=example.com ./healthcheck.sh
#

set -u

# --- Configuration -----------------------------------------------------------

HOST="${HOST:-localhost}"           # host to probe; override with HOST env var
TIMEOUT="${TIMEOUT:-3}"             # per-request timeout in seconds

# Ports come from CLI args if provided, otherwise use these defaults.
if [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; then
  PORTS=("$@")
else
  PORTS=(3000 8080)
fi

# --- Colors (only when stdout is a terminal) ---------------------------------

if [ -t 1 ]; then
  GREEN=$'\033[0;32m'
  RED=$'\033[0;31m'
  BOLD=$'\033[1m'
  RESET=$'\033[0m'
else
  GREEN="" ; RED="" ; BOLD="" ; RESET=""
fi

# --- Health check logic ------------------------------------------------------

# check_port <port>
# Returns 0 if the service responds, 1 otherwise.
check_port() {
  local port="$1"
  local url="http://${HOST}:${port}/"

  # curl flags:
  #   -s  silent, -S show errors, -o discard body
  #   --max-time bound total time; --connect-timeout bound connect phase
  # Any HTTP response (even 404) means the service is up and listening.
  if curl -sS -o /dev/null \
        --connect-timeout "$TIMEOUT" \
        --max-time "$TIMEOUT" \
        "$url" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    return 0
  fi
  return 1
}

# --- Main --------------------------------------------------------------------

echo "${BOLD}Health check — host: ${HOST}, timeout: ${TIMEOUT}s${RESET}"
echo "-----------------------------------------"

failures=0

for port in "${PORTS[@]}"; do
  if check_port "$port"; then
    printf '  %-6s %sUP%s\n'   "$port" "$GREEN" "$RESET"
  else
    printf '  %-6s %sDOWN%s\n' "$port" "$RED" "$RESET"
    failures=$((failures + 1))
  fi
done

echo "-----------------------------------------"

if [ "$failures" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "${GREEN}All ${#PORTS[@]} service(s) healthy.${RESET}"
  exit 0
else
  echo "${RED}${failures} of ${#PORTS[@]} service(s) DOWN.${RESET}"
  exit 1
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# healthcheck.sh - Check whether our services are running and responding.
#
# For each service we issue an HTTP request to its health endpoint and
# verify both that it connects AND that the response actually comes from
# our service (matching an expected token in the body). This avoids false
# positives from proxies / sandbox layers that may answer on the port but
# are not our application.
#
# Reports per-service status and exits non-zero if any service is down.
#
# Usage:
#   ./healthcheck.sh
#   HOST=example.com ./healthcheck.sh
#   TIMEOUT=5 ./healthcheck.sh
#

set -u

# --- Configuration -----------------------------------------------------------

HOST="${HOST:-localhost}"   # host to probe; override with HOST env var
TIMEOUT="${TIMEOUT:-3}"     # per-request timeout in seconds

# Each entry: "<name>|<port>|<path>|<expected-substring>"
# - name:              human-readable service label
# - port:              TCP port to probe
# - path:              URL path to request (health endpoint preferred)
# - expected-substring: text that must appear in the response body to
#                       confirm the response is genuinely from our service.
#                       Leave empty to accept any HTTP response.
SERVICES=(
  "api|3000|/health|\"status\":\"ok\""
  "web|8080|/health|\"status\":\"ok\""

#
# healthcheck.sh — Check whether local services are responding.
#
# Checks that the expected service ports accept connections (and, where

# and exits non-zero if any service is down.
#

#   ./healthcheck.sh

  "app:127.0.0.1:3000"
  "api:127.0.0.1:8080"

# Check a single TCP port. Returns 0 if reachable, 1 otherwise.
check_port() {
  local host="$1" port="$2"

  if command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    # --connect-timeout limits connection setup; we accept any HTTP reply.
    if curl --silent --show-error --output /dev/null \
            --connect-timeout "$TIMEOUT" "http://${host}:${port}/" 2>/dev/null; then
      return 0
    fi
    # curl returns non-zero for some HTTP statuses; re-check raw connectivity.
    if curl --silent --output /dev/null --connect-timeout "$TIMEOUT" \
            --write-out "%{http_code}" "http://${host}:${port}/" 2>/dev/null \
            | grep -qE '^[0-9]{3}$'; then

    fi

    nc -z -w "$TIMEOUT" "$host" "$port" >/dev/null 2>&1

    local rc=$?
    exec 3>&- 2>/dev/null || true
    return $rc
  fi
}

  echo "Health check — $(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')"
  echo "------------------------------------------"

    echo "${GREEN}All services healthy.${RESET}"
  else

    return 1

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# healthcheck.sh - Check whether local services are running.
#
# Probes a set of ports and reports whether each service responds.
# Exit code is 0 if all services are healthy, 1 if any are down.

set -uo pipefail

# Services to check: "label:host:port"
SERVICES=(
  "api:localhost:3000"
  "web:localhost:8080"
)

# How long (seconds) to wait for a connection before giving up.
TIMEOUT=3

# Color output only when stdout is a terminal.
if [[ -t 1 ]]; then
  GREEN=$'\033[0;32m'
  RED=$'\033[0;31m'
  BOLD=$'\033[1m'
  RESET=$'\033[0m'
else
  GREEN=""; RED=""; BOLD=""; RESET=""
fi

# check_port HOST PORT -> returns 0 if something is listening/responding
check_port() {
  local host="$1" port="$2"

  # Prefer an HTTP request if curl is available (confirms the service answers,
  # not just that the port is open).
  if command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    if curl -fsS --max-time "$TIMEOUT" "http://${host}:${port}/" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      return 0
    fi
    # Some endpoints return non-2xx at "/" but are still up; accept any HTTP reply.
    if curl -sS --max-time "$TIMEOUT" -o /dev/null "http://${host}:${port}/" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      return 0
    fi
    return 1
  fi

  # Fall back to a raw TCP connection check via bash's /dev/tcp.
  if timeout "$TIMEOUT" bash -c "exec 3<>/dev/tcp/${host}/${port}" 2>/dev/null; then
    return 0
  fi

  return 1
}

main() {
  echo "${BOLD}Service health check${RESET}"
  echo "--------------------"

  local failures=0

  for entry in "${SERVICES[@]}"; do
    IFS=':' read -r label host port <<< "$entry"

    if check_port "$host" "$port"; then
      printf '%-6s %s:%-5s  %sUP%s\n'   "$label" "$host" "$port" "$GREEN" "$RESET"
    else
      printf '%-6s %s:%-5s  %sDOWN%s\n' "$label" "$host" "$port" "$RED" "$RESET"
      failures=$((failures + 1))
    fi
  done

  echo "--------------------"
  if [[ "$failures" -eq 0 ]]; then
    echo "${GREEN}All services healthy.${RESET}"
    exit 0
  else
    echo "${RED}${failures} service(s) down.${RESET}"
    exit 1
  fi
}

# and reports their status.

#   ./healthcheck.sh                # check default ports (3000, 8080)
#   ./healthcheck.sh 3000 8080 9090 # check a custom list of ports

  local host="$1" port="$2"

    if curl -sS -o /dev/null --connect-timeout "$TIMEOUT" --max-time "$TIMEOUT" \

    return 0
  fi
  return 1
}

    printf "  Port %-6s ${GREEN}UP${RESET}\n" "$port"
  else
    printf "  Port %-6s ${RED}DOWN${RESET}\n" "$port"

  echo "${GREEN}${BOLD}All services healthy.${RESET}"
